b: My boyfriend [41M] and I [35F] have been together for 8 years. We have already talked this through, and we're okay. But something he said really hurt me, and I'm struggling to understand his perspective.

For context, I'm currently on sick leave after a pretty traumatic car accident where my wheel fell off my car as I was turning to get off the highway. I'm in constant pain, need weekly physiotherapy, and have significant medical expenses. I'm also worried about losing my job. Despite all this, I'm doing my best to stay positive, with the help of counseling.
We're also paying back a loan from my parents, who helped us buy our first little flat. We agreed to put aside 1,500 $ every month, meaning we're both living on a tighter budget than before.
My boyfriend recently commented that he sometimes feels I spend more money than I have, and that he's "not used to spending this much" compared to before we bought a place and moved in together.
When I asked what made him feel that way, he brought up two small outdoor Christmas trees I'd just bought for 29$.

I acknowledged they weren't necessary, but explained that my physiotherapist was away that week, so I'd decided to spend a little of the money I'd otherwise use for treatment on something that would make me happy.

Most days I'm in pain, exhausted, unable to socialize like I used to, and worried about my future. My counselor has encouraged me to do small things for myself occasionally, which would give a little extra joy, and I thought the trees would do just that by bringing a little extra coziness into our home.
What hurt me was the implication that I'm financially irresponsible.

I've always had a relatively low income and have even managed to save money during difficult periods. I haven't bought new clothes or shoes in probably two years, apart from a 9$ thrifted dress a few months ago.
When I asked for other examples, he mentioned plants, a cat bed, and gifts for friends and family. But these were things we'd agreed to buy together.

Since he's working and I'm on sick leave, I handle all the cooking and cleaning. We also agreed to up our food budget slightly more on groceries to eat healthier, anti-inflammatory meals, and I stay within that budget.

I even occasionally pay for shared household necessities like shampoo, toothbrush heads, and cleaning supplies out of my own pocket, without splitting the cost, so he has a little more money left to save.

He still has considerably more disposable income than I do after our shared expenses, although less than he was used to before our relationship. He's very savings-oriented, and I understand that adjusting to a tighter budget is difficult for him. Which is why I feel like it's fine, we need these shared things but I can get them because I don't mind. (I would like to add he is totally fine splitting the expenses, but I can see how it can sometimes stress him, and do I just do it here and there because it makes me happy to see him be like, yay, he could set so-and-so much aside this month.)

When we talked, he couldn't really explain why he saw me this way. He eventually said he didn't know why he'd said it, but that he just felt it, and it probably came out wrong because of course he didn't see me this wah. But he said he just couldn't understand buying Christmas decorations when I frequently have nothing left at the end of the month and I could have set the 29$ aside.
And I do understand his point. When money is tight and I'm worried about my job, saving that $29 would objectively be the more sensible decision.
But I also feel like there's a difference between occasionally buying something unnecessary and being someone who consistently spends beyond their means.

He apologized for hurting me, and we're not fighting. But I can't seem to shake the feeling that he's been quietly judging my spending habits, especially when so many of our purchases are mutual or related to my medical situation.
Now I feel guilty about the trees, and something that was supposed to bring me a little happiness just makes me sad. I'm even considering returning them.

This is my first long term relationship, and the first good and healthy relationship and I need a little advice going forward and help understanding where this came from. (Or if it is a normal thing for couples to "fight" about. We didn't fight just had an annoying discussion.)

I'd genuinely appreciate some outside perspectives. I feel this could be a result of financial stress for his part and having less money to save than he's used to? Or is there something about my spending that I'm not seeing? Logically I feel like he tells the truth when he says he didn't mean it. But I can't shake the feeling that this is how he sees me, apparently...
I love him, and I know he didn't intend to hurt me.

Endnote: He is very aware of making sure I have money set aside and means, in case we ever "broke up" as he says: it's important for women to have their own little fund just as a security reason. And he makes sure that I can actually afford to set aside to that, because we weigh our mutual expenses after income. Otherwise I wouldn't even be able to afford anything. But I do set aside, that's just part of my regular expenses.

TLDR; My boyfriend thinks I sometimes spend more money than I have, mainly because I bought $29 worth of Christmas decorations while on sick leave after a car accident. Most of my money goes toward medical expenses and shared necessities, and I rarely buy anything for myself. He couldn't really explain why he sees me this way, especially since most purchases he mentioned were mutually agreed upon. The comment hurt me deeper than I thought. I'm trying to understand his perspective and whether I'm missing something.
Edit: only to fix a bloop I missed in editing.

Second edit: I see people mentioning setting aside in general and I forgot to add into the original post, or perhaps phrased it completely wrong: That we do have a budget and set aside each of us, monthly, I just can't set that much aside given that we also set a lot aside each month, to pay back my parents quicker.
From reflecting on this, I know he probably just wanted me to set aside that little extra, to what I'm already saving.
What I use for physiotherapy etc. Is money that in our budget usually should be used for leisure, which I just don't have that much of recently.
